findings.title: Write lock taken without re-checking the cache, and held across manifest I/O
findings.description:
The read path at lines 41–47 takes the read lock, sees a nil cache (or dev mode), then takes the write lock at line 48 and unconditionally reloads (lines 51–70). There is no re-check after `Lock()`, so when N requests miss at cold start, each one in turn re-reads and re-parses `assets-manifest.json`. The same happens on persistent failure: if the manifest is missing, `result` is nil, the cache stays nil (line 69), and every request takes the exclusive lock and hits disk. Index and frontend-settings requests that previously ran concurrently now run one at a time. In dev mode every call falls through to the write lock, so all dev requests are serialized too.

Suggested fix: after `Lock()`, re-check `if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }`.

Holding the lock across I/O is acceptable today only because the CDN branch is dead (`cdn := ""`, line 54) and the file read is local. If the CDN path is enabled, the request at line 56 uses `http.DefaultClient`, which has no timeout. Every request's `RLock` at line 41 would wait on the write lock for as long as that fetch runs.

findings.title: No test covers the cache, the dev-mode bypass, or the new locking
findings.description:
`webassets_test.go` only tests `readWebAssetsFromFile` (`TestReadWebassets`) and a skipped CDN test (`TestReadWebassetsFromCDN`, line 90 `t.Skip()`). Nothing exercises `GetWebAssets`, so the cache-hit path, the dev-mode reload, and the `RWMutex` are untested. A regression would not be caught, and the race detector has nothing to run against.

Suggested test: set `cfg.StaticRootPath` to a temp dir containing `build/assets-manifest.json` (copied from `testdata/sample-assets-manifest.json`), use `licensingtest.FakeLicensing`, and call `GetWebAssets` from several goroutines under `go test -race`. Add a case with `Env: setting.Dev` to confirm reloads happen. The cache is a package global with no reset hook, so the test must clear `entryPointAssetsCache` under the lock between cases.

findings.title: The lock fixes an existing unsynchronized access to the global cache
findings.description:
Before this diff, concurrent HTTP handlers read and wrote `entryPointAssetsCache` with no synchronization, which is a data race. The new code reads under `RLock` and stores under `Lock`, so the race is gone. I checked the callers (`pkg/api/index.go:82`, `pkg/api/frontendsettings.go:62`, `pkg/middleware/recovery.go:141`). They only read the returned DTO. The DTO is fully built, including `SetContentDeliveryURL` at line 64, before it is published under the lock, so nothing mutates it once it is shared.

The deferred `Unlock` covers panics, which matters because `recovery.go:141` calls `GetWebAssets` from the panic path. None of the calls made under the write lock re-enter `GetWebAssets`: only `pkg/api` and `pkg/middleware` import `pkg/api/webassets`, and `pkg/setting` and `pkg/services/licensing` do not, so there is no re-entrant deadlock.
